key_numbers.metric: CodeBERT F1 gain from SCT-enhanced representation

structure_gain: SCALE (AST + LLM-generated comment tree) improves F1 by 1.17-13.47 points over best pre-trained/LLM baseline across three datasets (Table 3); RQ4 ablation shows removing SCT-Enhanced Representation module degrades performance.
confound_note: Main comparison (Table 3) varies both representation and underlying model architecture (SCALE-augmented UniXcoder vs. CodeBERT/CodeT5/ChatGPT baselines); RQ4 ablation (with/without SCTC, with/without SER) isolates representation components while holding the base encoder fixed.
stop_detail: ChatGPT-generated per-statement comments are inserted as sibling/parent nodes into a Tree-sitter AST via row-position matching, then 11 syntax-category rules replace AST node values with comment text to build the structured comment tree (Section 3.1-3.2).
threats_to_datum: Self-reported: limited to C/C++ (no Java/Python generalization claim), only 11 structured rules covering 4 statement categories, and evaluation restricted to models under 1B parameters (Section 6.2).

structure_gain: Repair success rises from 15% (no context) to 63% (full context-aware prompt combining CWE knowledge + structured code-context cues), a >4x improvement, same LLM (Copilot) throughout (Table I).
confound_note: Same LLM (GitHub Copilot) and same 156 snippets across all conditions; only prompt content varies in staged fashion (no context -> vulnerability disclosure -> CWE detail -> full structured context), isolating context amount as the manipulated variable.
stop_detail: Grounding is purely prompt-based: CWE description plus four structured code-context cues (buffer identification, bound selection, range precision, suitable placement) are progressively appended in a 'waterfall' staged prompt (Sections III-IV); no AST/CFG extraction performed.
threats_to_datum: No explicit threats-to-validity section; single commercial LLM (Copilot) tested, small custom dataset (156 snippets) with manual success labeling, and programming language not explicitly stated (examples appear C/C++).

key_numbers.metric: pAcc improvement of ReAct over Plain LLM

structure_gain: ReAct agent (interprocedural tool-use context via get_callers/get_callees/get_definition) raises pairwise accuracy from ~1-17.6% (Plain LLM) up to 19.13% (ReAct+CoT), but plain LLM retains higher raw F1 (65.96 vs 57-58), so the gain is metric-dependent (results table).
confound_note: Base LLMs (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini) held fixed across Plain LLM, Dependency-Augmented LLM, and ReAct Agent arms; context-acquisition strategy (none, fixed Top-5 similarity retrieval, adaptive agentic tool-use) is the manipulated factor, though effective context length/token budget differs by construction across arms.
stop_detail: ReAct agent grounds interprocedural reasoning via three callable tools built from CFlow-derived call graphs and CTags-extracted function bodies (get_callers, get_callees, get_definition), adaptively pulling context in a thought-action-observation loop (ReAct methodology section).
threats_to_datum: Vulnerability-introducing commit tracing may not perfectly reflect true origin given code evolution; label-balanced dataset may bias F1; ratio of interprocedural vulnerabilities not annotated due to cost; some model failures (Llama-3.1-8B) attributed to poor instruction-following rather than capability (Threats to Validity section).

datasets: Juliet Test Suite v1.3 (CWE-78, CWE-134, CWE-190, CWE-606 subsets)
structure_gain: Decompilation optimization (vulnerability-annotated, simplified, renamed pseudocode) plus memory-management agent yields ~10% average accuracy gain and up to ~37-point F1 gain (CWE-190) over LATTE baseline on Juliet binaries (Table 3); no controlled representation-only ablation is reported.
confound_note: Comparison is against a different tool (LATTE) entirely rather than a same-model ablation; decompilation-optimization representation, memory/context management, and underlying method all differ simultaneously between arms, so representation is not isolated.
stop_detail: GPT-4o annotates decompiled Ghidra pseudocode with vulnerability-flagging comments, simplifies control structures, and renames variables; a memory-management agent queues functions and stores/retrieves per-function summarized analysis in a SQL archival store to work around context-window limits (VulBinLLM architecture section, Figure 3).
threats_to_datum: Self-reported: binary vulnerability datasets are scarce, forcing evaluation on synthetic Juliet rather than real-world sets (BigVul, Devign) that are hard to compile consistently for binary analysis; no non-LLM or GNN-based binary baseline is compared.

datasets: custom (77 Verilog designs, 12 CWE types, mutation-synthesized)

key_numbers.metric: Illegal rule-usage rate with validation FSM

structure_gain: VeriPG graph (AST + control/data dependency) plus LLM-generated traversal rules improves F1 over LLM+external-knowledge baseline by 0.32 (GPT-4o: 0.57 vs 0.25) and 0.16 (DeepSeek-V3: 0.50 vs 0.34), same backbone LLMs held fixed (Table 2).
confound_note: Same two backbone LLMs (GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3) used across LLM-only, LLM+Knowledge, and VerilogLAVD arms; representation/context is the varied factor (raw code -> raw code+CWE text -> VeriPG graph+generated rules), though the full pipeline adds a rule-generation-and-traversal step beyond passive context.
stop_detail: LLM performs chain-of-thought extraction of vulnerability conditions from CWE text into JSON-structured rules (functions/filters/paths), symbolically executed via traversal over the VeriPG property graph, with a validation FSM checking primitive usage during rule generation (rule-generation and Table 3 sections).
threats_to_datum: No explicit threats-to-validity section; small dataset (77 designs, largely mutation-synthesized rather than real-world), single-module scope only, and no experimental comparison against traditional RTL security tools (e.g., Spyglass) due to unavailable code.

structure_gain: Neuro-symbolic loop (LLM source/sink inference + taint-path/CFG constraint validation) improves F1 to 79.6 vs 77.8 (IRIS) and 66.4 (static-only), cutting FPR to 17.5% vs 38.7% static-only (Table 1); no isolated raw-text-vs-structured ablation is reported.
confound_note: Central comparison is against distinct competing tools/pipelines (static-only, IRIS, FineWAVE, FuzzSlice, LLM4SA), not a same-model representation swap; internal component ablation (Table 2) removes whole modules (source/sink adaptation, FP filtering) rather than isolating representation type, and LLM backbone itself varies in one ablation arm (CodeLlama vs GPT-4).
stop_detail: LLM classifies candidate functions as source/sink/neutral from code snippets plus retrieved API docs, commit history, and comments; a separate constraint-validation stage checks static features (path length, sanitizer presence, control-flow feasibility) and a trained classifier filters spurious alerts, explicitly 'to avoid overreliance on LLMs' (neuro-symbolic architecture section).
threats_to_datum: Self-reported: LLM inference overhead, vulnerability to adversarial/misleading code comments biasing classification, limited explainability, and false negatives from LLM context-window truncation or implicit control flow.

datasets: Known Vulnerability Dataset (172 total / 162 test, from Brito et al.)
OSS Dataset (102 npm packages from top 5,000 by SourceRank)
structure_gain: LLM-derived taint specs (sources/sinks + repaired call graph) raise recall from 0% (CodeQL baseline, ruleset R1) to 65.43% (106/162) on known vulnerabilities; ablation (RQ3/Table IV) shows 76.4% of catches needed only custom sources/sinks while 23.6% additionally needed call-graph repair.
confound_note: CodeQL analysis engine held constant across rulesets R1-R7; varied factor is which LLM-derived representation component (sources/sinks vs repaired call graph vs both) is supplied, reasonably isolating representation contribution, though LLM backbone differs slightly per agent role (GPT-4 vs GPT-4-mini).
stop_detail: LLM-proposed facts (sources/sinks as endpoint locations, call edges as span locations) must bind by file/line/column to CodeQL's existing Data Flow Graph QL nodes; unbindable proposals are rejected, and each agent's output is aggregated across 3 runs via union or majority vote to reduce stochasticity (Validation subsection).
threats_to_datum: Self-reported: callback-mediated taint propagation unmodeled, TICR can miss calls across intra-procedural gaps, JS/npm-only scope, 1M-token limit excludes 21 large packages, dataset from June 2021 may not generalize to current code, and OSS filtering biases toward packages with prior GHSA records.

key_numbers.value: F1=0.93, P=0.95, R=0.92 vs best baseline F1=0.88 (Skill Scanner)
620 flagged, 400 manually confirmed malicious (64.5% precision open-world)

structure_gain: Full neuro-symbolic Skill Dependency Graph pipeline reaches F1=0.93 vs 0.88 best baseline on MalSkillsBench; ablation shows removing the symbolic extractor collapses recall to 0.27 and removing the neuro reasoner drops F1 to 0.71 with FPR rising to 0.49 (ablation table), same LLM backbone held fixed across arms.
confound_note: Baseline comparison (vs 5 community tools) runs different tools with the same LLM where applicable, but tools differ in overall pipeline, not representation alone; internal ablation (w/o symbolic/neuro extractor or reasoner) holds the LLM backbone (GPT-5.3-CodeX-Medium) fixed while varying which representation/reasoning component is active, more cleanly isolating representation contribution.
stop_detail: Security-sensitive operations extracted symbolically (Semgrep + YASA points-to/interprocedural data-flow) or via LLM from implicit NL cues are linked into a typed Skill Dependency Graph (artifact-contains-SSO-has_operand-value_flow edges); a neuro-to-symbolic feedback loop promotes stable LLM findings into symbolic rules over time (SDG construction / neuro-symbolic reasoning section).
threats_to_datum: Self-reported: MalSkillsBench may not capture full diversity of in-the-wild malicious skills, deep operand resolution limited to 4 languages (Python/JS/Java/Go), and attackers may adapt to reduce explicit security signals or exploit AI-evasion, degrading detection over time.

datasets: 178-bug benchmark (Yu et al.), 30 open-source C/C++ projects, 5k-1M SLOC

key_numbers.value: Kumushi preferred 47% vs Codex 27% (26% tied), sign test p=0.0065

structure_gain: Evidence-weighted ranked Functions-of-Interest context (call-graph traversal + dynamic traces + static dataflow) yields comparable oracle-based plausibility to Codex (85.4% vs 86.0%) but a higher root-cause-fix rate (84.9% vs 77.8%) and higher human preference (47% vs 27%) versus a frontier commercial coding agent lacking this pre-computed localization context (Section 4, Table 4).
confound_note: Comparison vs. Codex confounds localization/ranking advantage with other prompt-engineering and tooling differences, since Codex receives no pre-computed fault-localization context and no fix-quality guidelines; no controlled ablation isolates diversified localization vs. evidence-weighted ranking vs. presentation order alone.
stop_detail: Context is grounded via bounded bidirectional call-graph BFS (callers/callees) from crash-stack anchors, combined with AFL++ dynamic execution traces and static dataflow queries, consolidated into an evidence-weighted score ranking the top-20 Functions of Interest fed to the LLM alongside the sanitizer report (Section 3.1/3.3); patches are iteratively verified via ASan compilation, PoC replay, and test-suite execution, with failure output looped back to the agent (Section 3.3).
threats_to_datum: Self-reported: crash-anchored localization fails across opaque boundaries (e.g., bytecode encoding) with no static/dynamic path back to the true defect; fuzzer diversification may be insufficient within a 12-hour budget for narrow-trigger bugs; pipeline assumes sanitizer instrumentation and fuzzing infrastructure, limiting applicability beyond C/C++ (Section 6).

key_numbers.value: Claude: 15 vs 9 vs 9; GPT: 12 vs 8 vs 7

structure_gain: Removing either context source (local callee augmentation or repository-context bundle) roughly halves true-positive detections (Claude: 15->9/9; GPT: 12->8/7) at fixed LLM backbone (Table IV), directly isolating representation contribution.
confound_note: Table IV ablation holds the LLM backbone fixed (separately for Claude and GPT) and toggles context components (local augmentation, repo bundle) individually, a clean representation-only comparison; Table III's comparison to function-level and agentic baselines instead varies approach and context together.
stop_detail: Context-grounding is static and non-agentic: Tree-sitter extracts depth-one callee signatures/bodies and referenced macro/constant definitions (local augmentation), plus a once-per-repository five-section context bundle (system purpose, principal model, protected objects, information outputs, trust topology) serialized into a single structured LLM call per function (Section III-B, Fig. 1).
threats_to_datum: Self-reported: depth-one call-graph expansion may miss deeper interprocedural evidence, LLM sink identification can be incomplete or spurious, prioritization heuristic is imperfect and unproven optimal, small evaluation set (28 CVEs, 2 CWE types) may not generalize across languages or proprietary code (Section V).
